title: 12-Lead ECG
author: R. Castillo, MD
summary: Sinus tachycardia 118, PR 148 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT/QTc 320/448 ms. Tall, narrow T waves V2-V4 (potassium 5.4 at 0045).
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 118 bpm. PR 148 ms. QRS 88 ms. QT/QTc 320/448 ms.

**Interpretation**
Sinus tachycardia. Tall, narrow T waves in V2 to V4. P waves present, PR and QRS normal: no signs of severe hyperkalemia. No ST changes, no arrhythmia.

**Context**
DKA, potassium 5.4 at 0045 (resulted 0130). No potassium in the fluids until K is 5.0 or lower; recheck in 2 hours. Insulin will move potassium into the cells: the total body potassium is low.
impression: Sinus tachycardia 118 with tall T waves V2-V4, consistent with potassium 5.4. QTc 448 ms.

title: 12-Lead ECG
author: P. Raman, MD
summary: Sinus rhythm 92, PR 152 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT/QTc 378/468 ms. Flattened T waves with prominent U waves V2-V3 (potassium 3.3 at 1830).
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 92 bpm. PR 152 ms. QRS 88 ms. QT/QTc 378/468 ms (measured to the end of the T wave; the U wave makes the end of repolarization hard to see).

**Interpretation**
Normal sinus rhythm. Low, flat T waves with rounded U waves after them, best in V2 and V3. No ectopy. Compared with 0115: rate slower (118 to 92), the tall T waves are gone and a low-potassium pattern has appeared.

**Context**
Potassium 5.4 (0045), 4.6 (0300), 4.1 (0630), 3.8 (1030), 3.6 (1430), 3.3 (1830) on the insulin infusion; magnesium 1.7. Insulin infusion held at 1920; potassium chloride riders 10 mEq/h through the second IV; magnesium 2 g. STAT BMP 2130. Keep on the cardiac monitor.
impression: Normal sinus rhythm 92. Flattened T waves and U waves, consistent with potassium 3.3. No arrhythmia.
